ideas.title: Extension system and marketplace for custom integrations
ideas.title_zh: 扩展系统与扩展市场
ideas.problem: Asks for a formal extension system so integrations, for example local model providers or custom context sources, do not have to live in the core repo. The thread is open, and later plugin proposals reference it.

sources.title: [Feature]: [RFC] Extension System / Marketplace for custom integrations
Plugins: a working build to try before you settle the design

mount_today.note: There is no plugin API to build on; the discussion is the request for one.

ideas.title: Lifecycle hooks, settings and UI contributions for extensions
ideas.title_zh: 扩展的生命周期钩子、设置与界面贡献
ideas.problem: Asks for a Pi-style extension API where integrations react to app and agent lifecycle events such as a turn settling, expose their own settings, and add small UI pieces like a status indicator, so no fork is needed.

sources.title: [Feature]: Pi-style extension API for lifecycle hooks, UI contributions, and settings

mount_today.note: Hooks and UI contributions need a host API; Custom CSS, MCP and Skills cannot react to app lifecycle events.

ideas.title: Plugin-contributed right-panel surfaces with a waiting count
ideas.title_zh: 插件可贡献的右侧面板与等待计数
ideas.problem: One commenter reports a downstream fork that adds eight right-panel surfaces through a small registry, which takes about 18 small edits to wire into upstream, and suggests a first slice limited to plugin-contributed panel surfaces with an optional waiting count. Single source.

sources.title: Right-panel registry as a first plugin slice (comment by CantrellJax on #31472)

mount_today.note: The docs list no entry that registers a panel surface.

ideas.title: Hover cards for ticket numbers in messages and thread titles
ideas.title_zh: 消息与线程标题中工单号的悬浮卡片
ideas.problem: A commenter who built a plugin on the open plugin branch wants a hook that registers a text pattern such as ABC-1234 and supplies a hover card for matches, instead of depending on how T3 renders text. Single source.

sources.title: Hover card hook for ticket numbers (comment by lizzy-thornton on #31472)

mount_today.note: Matching text and drawing a card inside the chat needs a rendering hook; Custom CSS cannot read text or fetch ticket data.

ideas.title: Status line, composer bar and slash-command panes from local mods
ideas.title_zh: 本地 mod 提供状态栏、输入框上方栏与斜杠命令面板
ideas.problem: Proposes local mods, small folders of code that add a pane beside the chat, a bar above the composer, a status line or a slash command, working with any provider. The author says it runs on their own machine; the thread has no comments.

sources.title: Mods: your own interface inside T3 Code, the same with every model
Status-line item for subscription usage pace (comment by Anneo22 on #6837)

mount_today.note: The docs list no entry that adds a bar or pane; Custom CSS styles existing elements (docs/user/appearance.md).

ideas.title: Switchable CSS snippets that load after the theme
ideas.title_zh: 可单独开关、在主题之后加载的 CSS 片段
ideas.problem: Suggests user stylesheets as the smallest useful first slice: a folder of .css files switched on in Settings → Appearance, loaded after the theme, with stable data attributes for the main window regions. Single source.

sources.title: User stylesheets as a first slice (comment by pouyarezvani on #31472)

mount_today.note: A theme's Custom CSS is applied after T3's own styles (docs/user/appearance.md), so one snippet can ship as a theme today. Switching several snippets on and off independently is what is missing.

ideas.title: Opt-in shader effects as feedback to composer interaction
ideas.title_zh: 可选的输入交互着色器反馈效果
ideas.problem: Proposes opt-in effects that react to interaction, such as droplets on keystrokes, a wave on send and a ripple on completion, explicitly not running constantly because of battery cost. The author offers to upstream it.

sources.title: Opt-in, tasteful and occasional shader-driven effects in the UI

mount_today.note: Custom CSS is styling only (docs/user/appearance.md). Effects driven by keystrokes need script access to the page; CSS animations could only approximate them.

ideas.title: Collapse or hide inline MCP app cards per server
ideas.title_zh: 按服务器折叠或隐藏对话内的 MCP 应用卡片
ideas.problem: MCP apps render inline in Claude threads, and the report shows a Jira app asking for cards up to 2,000px tall with no collapse control. Two discussions ask for a per-server collapse-by-default or a hide option.

sources.title: Per-server "collapse by default" for MCP Apps (Atlassian's Jira cards take over Claude threads)
Allow collapsing or hiding inline MCP app cards while keeping the connector enabled

mount_today.note: Custom CSS could only help if cards carried a stable data attribute. In apps/web/src/components/chat/McpAppFrame.tsx on main (read 2026-11-19) the only one is data-mcp-app-fullscreen, so it is not dependable.

ideas.title: Dashboard of threads waiting on you, across projects
ideas.title_zh: 跨项目的“等你处理”线程看板
ideas.problem: Commenters on the extension-API thread describe a sidebar card per project showing its waiting-on-you queue and a coordinator dashboard across threads. Both are single comments.

sources.title: Per-project waiting-on-you card (comment by Anneo22 on #6837)
Action list and coordinator dashboard (comment by P4rcev4l on #6837)

mount_today.note: The official MCP server lets outside agents read projects and threads (docs/user/outside-agents.md). The t3buddy README (read 2026-11-19) says its macOS companion shows live thread state, including threads waiting on an answer, through T3's MCP server.

ideas.title: System tray or menu-bar icon for background status
ideas.title_zh: 系统托盘或菜单栏状态图标
ideas.problem: With T3 Code running in the background there is no system-level indicator of whether it, its backend and the local T3 Connect environment are still up. The request is a tray or menu-bar icon with status and basic controls.

sources.title: [Feature]: Add a system tray or menu-bar icon for background status and controls

mount_today.note: A separate companion app can read thread status over the official MCP server, as the t3buddy README (read 2026-11-19) describes for a desktop HUD. Lifecycle controls such as stopping the server are not among the tools listed in docs/user/outside-agents.md.

ideas.title: Git history view for the active project
ideas.title_zh: 当前项目的 Git 历史视图
ideas.problem: There is no obvious way to browse past commits inside T3 Code. The request lists a commit list with author and date, the files changed by a commit, and a diff, starting from local history only.

sources.title: [Feature]: Add a Git history view

mount_today.note: A separate local page can read git log and diffs itself and use the project list from the official MCP server. Whether it can be opened inside T3, for example in its browser panel, was not tested.

ideas.title: Version-control panel for branches, worktrees, stashes and remotes
ideas.title_zh: 分支、工作树、暂存与远端的版本控制面板
ideas.problem: Agents create branches, worktrees and commits faster than they can be tracked, and the author still opens another Git client to see which branches are ahead or behind, stashes, and remote branches.

sources.title: Review and act on working trees, branches and remotes from a Version Control panel

mount_today.note: A separate local page can read branch, worktree and stash state from git for the projects the official MCP server lists. It would sit outside T3's own UI.

ideas.title: Skill manager across every provider's skill folders
ideas.title_zh: 跨各提供方 skill 目录的 Skill 管理
ideas.problem: Skills live in different directories per provider, so users end up with duplicated copies that drift or skills only one provider sees. T3 already scans these locations for the $ picker but offers no way to see the gaps.

sources.title: Skill manager: view, add, edit, and link skills across every harness

mount_today.note: A Skill can tell an agent to scan the skill folders the issue lists and report duplicates and drift. It is a report, not an editing UI. T3 lists skills enabled for the provider via the $ picker (docs/user/composer.md).

ideas.title: Provider-neutral project memory that agents write and you can inspect
ideas.title_zh: 各提供方通用、可查看可删除的项目记忆
ideas.problem: Each provider keeps its own memory or only instruction files, so what an agent learned does not survive a new thread or a provider switch. The T3 MCP server has thread and project tools but nothing that persists notes.

sources.title: Project memory that agents can write, recall, and you can see and delete

mount_today.note: A notes MCP server added to the provider gives agents write and recall tools today; restart the agent session after adding it (docs/user/composer.md). Viewing and deleting notes would be through that server, not a T3 screen.

ideas.title: Read assistant replies aloud
ideas.title_zh: 朗读助手回复
ideas.problem: Asks for a per-message read-aloud action using the browser speech API or an optional cloud voice, for reading while away from the screen. A later commenter on the extension-API thread also lists read-aloud of replies.

sources.title: [Feature]: Read AI responses aloud via built-in TTS (per-message "read aloud" action)
Read-aloud of replies as an extension use case (comment by P4rcev4l on #6837)

mount_today.note: A per-message button needs a UI hook. An MCP app (docs/user/html-renders.md) could speak text it is handed, but whether its sandbox allows speech synthesis was not tested.

ideas.title: Token usage and estimated cost per thread
ideas.title_zh: 按线程显示 token 用量与估算费用
ideas.problem: Asks for each thread to show total tokens split into input, output and cache, an estimated API cost marked as not a bill, and a per-model breakdown. The Usage page documents per-model breakdowns; thread-level totals are not described there.

sources.title: Show token usage and estimated cost per thread

mount_today.note: Per-thread numbers sit in provider history that T3 reads for the Usage page (docs/user/usage.md); docs/user/outside-agents.md does not list a usage tool.

ideas.title: Expose remaining provider quota through the MCP server
ideas.title_zh: 通过 MCP 服务暴露各提供方剩余额度
ideas.problem: With several Codex and Claude accounts, the author wants the MCP server to list each account's remaining 5-hour and weekly quota so an orchestrating agent can delegate to the account with the most left.

sources.title: Expose the current provider usage via mcp

mount_today.note: It needs a new tool on T3's own MCP server; docs/user/outside-agents.md lists projects, threads, providers and models, not quota.

ideas.title: Per-thread cost and budget from a proxy's own prices
ideas.title_zh: 按代理自身价格显示线程费用与预算
ideas.problem: For a Claude instance behind a LiteLLM proxy, the author wants the cost so far in the thread priced from the proxy's rates and the remaining budget in Limits, because Usage uses a public rate table and mixes accounts. Single source.

sources.title: Per-thread cost and budgets for Claude instances behind a LiteLLM proxy, read from the proxy's API

mount_today.note: Pricing a thread needs both T3's session data and a place to show the result in the thread; the proxy side already exposes spend and budgets over its API, per the post.

ideas.title: Wake a thread when a watched command prints something
ideas.title_zh: 被监视命令有输出时唤醒线程
ideas.problem: Pull-request watching exists, but nothing like it for other waits such as a discussion reply or a deploy. The author's workaround is an external cron job that sends a message into the thread, which T3 cannot see or stop.

sources.title: Wake a thread when a command prints something (`watch_command`)

mount_today.note: A script on the host can already message a thread with t3 thread send (docs/user/outside-agents.md), which is the discussion's workaround. T3 still cannot show or cancel the watch.

ideas.title: Manual, collapsible thread groups with optional colors
ideas.title_zh: 可手动分组、可折叠并带颜色的线程组
ideas.problem: A project is not always the right organizing unit, so the request is user-created named groups inside a project, collapsible, with optional colors and an activity indicator on a collapsed group. The sidebar docs list a group-by-project mode (docs/user/thread-sidebar.md), which is not manual grouping.

sources.title: Manual, collapsible thread groups with optional colors

mount_today.note: Groups need stored data and sidebar logic; Custom CSS cannot know which thread belongs to which group.

ideas.title: Pin agent responses in a thread and jump between pins
ideas.title_zh: 在线程中固定回复并在固定项间跳转
ideas.problem: Long threads bury the few answers that matter, such as the agreed plan or a root cause. The request is a pin action on a message, a per-thread pin list, and next and previous pin keybindings.

sources.title: Pin agent responses in a thread and jump between pins

mount_today.note: No documented open entry adds a per-message action or stores a pin list.

ideas.title: On-demand cloud sandbox environments through pluggable providers
ideas.title_zh: 按需创建云端沙箱环境的可插拔提供方
ideas.problem: Asks for environments created on demand for each task or worktree through a user-configured sandbox broker or per-backend drivers (Boat, Daytona and similar), so no always-on server has to be kept. T3 would then connect through its existing remote or pairing flow. Two separate posts describe the same need; counts are not added.

sources.title: [Feature]: On-demand cloud task environments through an external sandbox broker
Provision sandbox environments from Settings (Boat, Daytona, Vercel, Upstash, Celesto + any driver)

mount_today.note: Creating and tearing down environments needs a host hook; MCP, Skills and Custom CSS cannot add an environment provider.

ideas.title: Pluggable workspace providers instead of a fixed git worktree
ideas.title_zh: 可插拔的工作区提供方（不止 git worktree）
ideas.problem: Asks for pluggable create and remove commands for a thread's isolated workspace, for example copy-on-write clones or Worktrunk, with support for non-git directories and cleanup when a thread settles. A second post offers a Worktrunk integration as an optional worktree manager.

sources.title: Workspace providers: pluggable create/remove commands (rift, CoW clones, Worktrunk), with support for non-git directories and cleanup on settle
Should I submit my Git/worktree workflow improvements to upstream?

mount_today.note: Workspace creation is built into the server; no official open entry lets an outside tool replace it.

ideas.title: Extension point for custom source control providers
ideas.title_zh: 自定义代码托管提供方的扩展点
ideas.problem: Asks for a minimal extension point so CLI-backed providers can add change-request features (create, list, status, checkout) for hosts that T3 does not recognize, such as an internal review system, without keeping a fork. Single source.

sources.title: Pluggable source control providers (custom CLI-backed providers for unsupported hosts)

mount_today.note: The provider list is a closed set in the app's contracts; nothing official lets a third party add one.

ideas.title: Outbound webhooks and local hooks for turn and thread events
ideas.title_zh: 回合与线程事件的外发 webhook 与本地钩子
ideas.problem: Asks for a user-configurable outbound callback when a turn or thread reaches a terminal state, so supervisors, CI or local notifiers (sound or desktop alerts) can react. Scheduled tasks can already be triggered by an inbound webhook; this is the opposite direction. Two posts, counts not added.

sources.title: Feature: configurable outbound completion webhook for turn/thread terminal events
Feature request: local lifecycle hooks / notification integration for tools like peon-ping

mount_today.note: There is no official outbound event or hook surface to subscribe to; polling through MCP was not tested.

ideas.title: Local app SDK and URL-backed custom project surfaces
ideas.title_zh: 本地应用 SDK 与按网址挂载的自定义面板
ideas.problem: An RFC for a typed client over the server's existing endpoints and an "Add plugin" surface that opens your own web app inside T3 and hands it a one-time code, so the page can read threads and dispatch turns. The author marks the original text as outdated and reduces it to an MVP. Single source.

sources.title: [RFC]: Local app integration SDK and custom project surfaces MVP

mount_today.note: Embedding your own page as a panel needs a host surface; a standalone page beside T3 is not the same thing.

ideas.title: Quota-aware account selection and automatic fallback provider
ideas.title_zh: 按剩余额度选账号并在触顶时自动换提供方
ideas.problem: Asks T3 to track remaining quota per account and pick the one with the most headroom for a new task, and to hand off to a configured fallback provider when a usage limit is hit instead of waiting for the reset. Two posts, counts not added.

sources.title: Option to automatically hand off to a fallback provider when hitting usage limits
[Feature]: Auto-select the account with the most remaining quota before starting a task

mount_today.note: Switching account or provider mid-thread needs a host API; MCP can read usage once exposed, but cannot change the thread's provider.

ideas.title: Discord Rich Presence for coding activity
ideas.title_zh: 把编码状态显示到 Discord 的 Rich Presence
ideas.problem: Proposes an off-by-default desktop setting that publishes project name, model or agent activity through the local Discord client. The author asked the maintainers for scope approval before continuing. Single source.

sources.title: Optional desktop Discord Rich Presence (scope approval request)

mount_today.note: A desktop-side integration that reads thread activity needs an official event source.

ideas.title: Safe login fill for the preview browser
ideas.title_zh: 预览浏览器里的安全登录填充
ideas.problem: Two posts describe testing apps that need a login in the preview browser: one asks for project-scoped test credential profiles that agents can use without the secret crossing the model boundary, the other for a password manager (Enpass) extension. The official docs describe a 1Password secret provider and private secret requests; neither post is about that path. Counts not added.

sources.title: Secure project-scoped credential profiles for preview-browser test logins
Fill logins from Enpass in the preview browser

mount_today.note: Filling fields in the embedded browser needs a host hook; untested whether the existing secret requests could carry it.

ideas.title: Compact per-turn stats footer
ideas.title_zh: 每回合的紧凑统计页脚
ideas.problem: Asks for a small row under each response showing model and effort, tokens per second, token count, time to first token and tool-call count, so a long coding run is easy to audit. Single source.

sources.title: [Feature]: Add compact per-turn session stats footer

mount_today.note: Adding to the message footer needs a host UI contribution point.

ideas.title: Saved prompt snippets in the composer
ideas.title_zh: 输入框里的常用提示词片段
ideas.problem: Asks for named, optionally grouped snippets that are searchable from the composer and inserted into the draft without sending, for repeated PR, review or CI prompts. Single source.

sources.title: [Feature]: Saved snippets for frequently used prompts, with optional grouping

mount_today.note: A Skill can carry a repeated prompt, but it is not an insert-only draft snippet; a composer extension would be needed.

ideas.title: Import and continue sessions from Claude Code and Codex
ideas.title_zh: 导入并接续 Claude Code、Codex 的会话
ideas.problem: Asks to browse sessions stored by Claude Code or Codex on the same machine, resume them in T3 with their history, and optionally continue them in the CLI afterwards. One post notes the Codex files already sit in the local sessions folder. Two posts, counts not added.

sources.title: [Feature]: continue threads from claude code
request: import or recreate sessions from Codex

mount_today.note: Creating a thread with imported history needs a host API; the user docs only describe importing from older T3 versions and browsers.

ideas.title: Wake or snooze a thread on pull request events
ideas.title_zh: 按 PR 事件唤醒或暂缓线程
ideas.problem: Asks for a snooze mode that keeps a thread out of the way until its linked pull request gets a review, comment, check result or conflict, and for waking a watched thread when the PR merges or a review bot reacts. Pull request watching exists in the docs; these are the waits it does not cover. Two posts, counts not added.

sources.title: Snooze a thread until its pull request changes
Wake a watched PR's thread when it merges or closes, and when a review bot reacts

mount_today.note: Waking a thread needs host thread control; MCP tools cannot snooze or wake a thread from outside.
